components.gap: Item-by-item comparison with the held article (printed pp. 56-68) finds these source items missing or altered on the route. (1) p. 56, opening paragraph: the justificatory claim that the partial incorporation of lambda-conversion 'has certain advantages from the point of view of type theory and is offered as being of interest on this basis', with the hedge 'whatever may be thought of the finally satisfactory character of the theory of types as a foundation for logic and mathematics', is absent; 040:5-27 and the boundary note 040:911-913 keep only that a complete incorporation is impossible. (2) p. 56: the historical attribution that the features not connected with lambda-conversion are owed to Whitehead and Russell, Hilbert and Ackermann, Hilbert and Bernays and their forerunners (nn. 3-5) is absent. (3) p. 56 n. 1: the historical claim that the simple theory of types was suggested as a modification of Russell's ramified theory by Chwistek (1921, 1922) and by Ramsey (1926), with the pointer to Carnap's Abriss der Logistik, is absent, as is n. 2's pointer to Church's Mathematical logic (1936) and The calculi of lambda-conversion. (4) p. 56, §1: the source's third type-abbreviation example, 'iota iota (iota iota)' for '((iota iota)(iota iota))', is replaced at 040:42-45 by a different example, 'iota(iota iota)' for '(iota(iota iota))', which is cited to [§1, p. 56] although the source does not contain it. (5) p. 57, §1: the claim that 'the matter of interpretation is in any case irrelevant to the abstract construction of the theory' and the qualification '(formal consistency assumed)' attached to the possibility of other and quite different interpretations are absent; 040:166-168 keeps only that the nature of o and iota is left open and other interpretations are admitted. (6) p. 63, §5: the scope qualification on 21^(alpha beta), 'no use will be made of them below because we shall be concerned entirely with consequences of 1-9^alpha', is absent at 040:357-380. (7) p. 61, §4: the justification of the formal/syntactical-theorem distinction as 'a necessary part of the process of using a known language (English) to set up another (more exact) language' is absent at 041:605-610.

components.gap: Three results stated in the source have no written proof on the route. (1) p. 59: that the same-type predecessor P_(alpha' alpha') cannot be defined without descriptions, which the source derives from the independence of the axiom of infinity (§4); the handbook reports it as an unproved source claim (040:162-166, 041:617-632, 034:624-632) and does not carry out that derivation, although it proves the independence of Axioms 7 and 8. (2) p. 61: that Axioms 10^(alpha beta) are 'nevertheless adequate' because the class of F_(o alpha) can be taken as lambda x_alpha (iota y_iota') . (F x)[y = 0_iota'] v (not F x)[y = 1_iota']; 040:305-315 reports the source's argument, but no derivation shows that coextensive propositional functions receive equal classes under this representation (which needs 9^(iota'), 10 and 0_iota' distinct from 1_iota'). (3) p. 64: the announced result that 26^(iota'), 26^(iota''), ... are consequences of 1-6^alpha and 8 is not established; the written derivation uses Axiom 7 through 28^alpha and 27^iota, and 040:489-499 with annex 040:643-650 state that removing Axiom 7 is not settled.

components.gap: The reconstruction misattributes and omits source content. At 040:42-45 the handbook cites [§1, p. 56] for the example 'iota(iota iota) abbreviates (iota(iota iota))', which the source does not give, and does not reconstruct the source's own example 'iota iota(iota iota)' for '((iota iota)(iota iota))'. The source's actual cited boundaries in nn. 1-5 (Carnap; Chwistek and Ramsey as originators of the simple theory; Church's own lambda-conversion works; Whitehead-Russell, Hilbert-Ackermann and Hilbert-Bernays as the sources of the features not tied to lambda-conversion) are not preserved, and the opening justificatory claim is not carried, so the bridge does not cover the whole presentation (see N-a-071-S01-PRESENTATION).
